$comment: GENERATED by core scripts/agent-tool-catalog.cjs (npm run catalog:agent) - never edit by hand.

generator.source: tpAgent.tools() via core scripts/agent-tool-catalog.cjs, mapped by tools/agent/src/catalog.js

instructions:
You are building in the person's own open theprototype.app tab: a live, shared 3D scene. Every change shows for everyone in the session and can be undone.
This may be a VOICE conversation: answer in one or two short spoken sentences and say what changed in plain words ("Added three trees by the fire"). Never read out uuids, lists of numbers or JSON.
If a tool says the tab is closed or not connected, tell the person to open theprototype.app and press Connect Claude, then wait; do not retry in a loop.
Call status first: it says whether you may edit (a viewer can only look).
Call list_scene before editing so you use real uuids; batch many objects into one call.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.
Use screenshot to check a result when it matters, not after every step.
When asked what you can do here, call what_can_you_do and say its "say" line.

tools.name: list_scene
tools.title: Read the scene
tools.description: List every object currently in the scene with its uuid, name, type, parent, transform, material, color and (for a primitive) its shape — geometry {type, sizes such as the thickness of a wall}. Call this before editing so you use real uuids. On a big scene narrow it: brief (uuids + names only), name (a glob), type, near {position, radius}. A big flow graph shows its first page and says how to read the rest: pass {flow: "scene" | object uuid, page} to read one page of one graph.

flow.description: optional: read one flow graph ("scene" or an object uuid) page by page instead of the scene summary

brief.description: optional: only uuid, name, type, parentUuid per object (cheap on a big scene)

name.description: optional: only objects whose name matches — a glob ("Wall*", "*door*"), or plain text = contains; case-insensitive

type.description: optional: only objects of this type — Mesh, Group, PointLight… or a primitive shape (Box, Wall, Sphere…)

near.description: optional: only objects within radius of a WORLD position

tools.name: create_objects
tools.title: Add objects
tools.description: Create one or more primitives, lights or empty groups in a single call. Ground is the y=0 plane; place objects so they rest ON it (a box of height h sits at y=h/2). Returns the new uuids.

params.description: up to 4 constructor args. Box=[w,h,d], Sphere=[radius], Cylinder=[rTop,rBottom,height], Cone=[radius,height], Plane=[w,h], Torus=[radius,tube]. Omit for sensible defaults.

color.description: hex like #ff8800 (a mesh, or a light's colour)

intensity.description: lights: brightness (point/spot also fall off with distance)

aim.description: directional/spot: a world point [x,y,z] to point at

parentUuid.description: uuid of an existing group to nest under — position/rotation/scale are then LOCAL to that group

physics.description: default static (it stays put in Play). dynamic = it falls, collides and can be thrown — only when asked for

tools.name: update_objects
tools.title: Change objects
tools.description: Modify existing objects by uuid: move/rotate/scale, recolor, change material, rename, show/hide, or reparent. Batch many in one call.

materialParams.description: meshes: numbers (roughness, metalness, opacity, emissiveIntensity, clearcoat, transmission, ior, shininess…, clamped), true/false (wireframe, transparent, flatShading), hex colours (emissive, specular), side (front|back|double), and map = a library image hash (null clears). Each bad key comes back in errors.

intensity.description: lights: brightness (point/spot also fall off with distance)

aim.description: directional/spot: a world point [x,y,z] to point at

parentUuid.description: group uuid to nest under, or "root" to un-nest. The object keeps its world pose; a position given in the same update is LOCAL to the new parent

tools.name: delete_objects
tools.title: Delete objects
tools.description: Delete objects by uuid.

tools.name: group_objects
tools.title: Group objects
tools.description: Create a new group and move the given member objects into it. Returns the group uuid.

tools.name: clear_scene
tools.title: Clear the scene
tools.description: Delete ALL objects in the scene. Requires confirm:true. Use only when the user clearly asks to start over.

tools.name: animate_parts
tools.title: Animate parts
tools.description: Animate a model's NAMED PARTS (child nodes from list_scene: a rotor, a door, a lid) with one clip — e.g. spin a rotor: tracks [{part: 'rotor', keys: [{t: 0, rot: [0, 0, 0]}, {t: 1, rot: [0, 360, 0]}]}], loop true. Keys are offsets from each part's rest pose (mode 'relative', the default; 'absolute' = local values). rot is Euler degrees [x, y, z]; pos metres [x, y, z]; scale a factor. The clip is saved as a .tpanim file, plays on every peer, and is one undo step.

object.description: the model: its uuid (from list_scene) or exact name

loop.description: repeat (default true); false = play once and hold

tools.name: set_material
tools.title: Change materials and textures
tools.description: Make objects look finished: colour, roughness, metalness, emissive, opacity and texture maps, on many objects in one call. Maps take a library image hash or an https URL (https only, CORS-enabled, 16 MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/AVIF; it becomes a library item first and is re-encoded like an upload; returned in assets). cc0 fetches a free CC0 material by name (Poly Haven / ambientCG); preset applies a named preset. faces gives just those faces their own new material slot. One undo step.

color.description: base colour: hex or a CSS name

emissive.description: glow colour: hex or a CSS name

params.description: any other material number, e.g. {"clearcoat": 1, "transmission": 0.9, "ior": 1.5} (those need type MeshPhysicalMaterial)

maps.description: texture slots, each a library image hash, an https URL, or null to clear

cc0.description: a CC0 material by name, e.g. "Wood051" or "brown planks"

slot.description: which material slot of a multi-material object (default 0)

faces.description: which faces: {"normal": "up"|"down"|"+x"|"-x"|"+z"|"-z"|[x,y,z], "angle": 30}, {"box": {"min": [..], "max": [..]}} (local space), {"indices": [..]} or {"all": true}; filters AND together

tools.name: list_materials
tools.title: Read materials
tools.description: What objects wear: per object its material slots (type, colour, numbers, which maps) and shader, plus the preset names and shader keys. Read this before editing.

name.description: only objects whose name contains this

tools.name: get_material
tools.title: Read one material
tools.description: One object's material in full: every slot, each map's tiling / offset / rotation / size / hash, and its shader graph as text with the uniforms a flow can drive.

tools.name: create_shader
tools.title: Give objects a shader
tools.description: Give objects a node shader, written as text like flow graphs: one line per node (id = type {param: value}), one per edge (source[.output] -> target.input), ending at a "surface" node. Example: c = color {value: "#ff8800"}\nout = surface\nc -> out.emissive. Call describe_shader_nodes for the types. Each object gets its own copy. Compiler errors come back in the result and nothing is written. Returns the graph key and its uniforms: a float one (u_<nodeId>_<param>) can be driven by a flow "setuniform" node on that object. scene: true makes the default for every object, which asks the host first.

replace.description: replace a graph the object already has

scene.description: the scene default instead of objects (asks the host)

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

tools.name: edit_shader
tools.title: Edit a shader
tools.description: Change a shader graph: params [{node, param, value}] for values, add (text: new or replaced nodes, new edges), removeNodes, or text for the whole graph. Errors come back and nothing changes.

shader.description: the key from create_shader or list_materials

add.description: text: nodes to add or replace and edges to add

tools.name: assign_shader
tools.title: Copy or remove a shader
tools.description: Copy an existing shader graph onto objects (each gets its own copy), or take a shader off with shader: null.

shader.description: the key of the graph to copy, or null to remove

tools.name: describe_shader_nodes
tools.title: Look up shader node types
tools.description: The shader node catalog: each type with what it does, its params (which become uniforms), inputs and outputs.

tools.name: set_post
tools.title: Change the post effects
tools.description: The scene's post effects (bloom, huesaturation, brightnesscontrast, tonemapping, vignette, grain, chromaticaberration, ao, lut, pixelation, scanlines, dotscreen, smaa; get_post lists every param). effects: [{kind, params, enabled, at, remove}], matched to what is there by id or kind, so repeating a call does not stack a second bloom; replace: true drops the rest; the stack order is the order of effect. This changes the whole scene's look: the first call returns needsConfirm and the host is asked; repeat it with confirmId. One undo step.

enabled.description: the whole stack on or off

camera.description: a camera's own look instead of the scene's

mode.description: camera look: add to the scene look, or replace it

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

tools.name: get_post
tools.title: Read the post effects
tools.description: The look stack as it is (effects with ids and params) and every effect kind with its params and ranges.

camera.description: a camera's own look instead of the scene's

tools.name: create_post_graph
tools.title: Add a custom post effect
tools.description: A custom post effect: a preset, or a shader graph as text ending at a "postOutput" node (describe_shader_nodes domain post), added to the look. Changes the whole scene's look, so it asks the host first like set_post. Compiler errors come back in the result.

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

tools.name: uv_unwrap
tools.title: Unwrap UVs
tools.description: New texture coordinates: smart (flat islands by surface direction, the default), box, planar, cylindrical, spherical. faces limits it to those faces and leaves the rest. Use it when a texture smears on a model. One undo step.

faces.description: which faces: {"normal": "up"|"down"|"+x"|"-x"|"+z"|"-z"|[x,y,z], "angle": 30}, {"box": {"min": [..], "max": [..]}} (local space), {"indices": [..]} or {"all": true}; filters AND together

tools.name: set_uv
tools.title: Set texture tiling or face mapping
tools.description: Tile, shift or rotate a material slot's textures (tiling: 4 repeats a floor texture four times). maps limits it to some slots. With faces it maps only those faces instead: they are projected flat so the image fills them once (a label on one side of a box), with tiling / offset / rotation on top; pair it with set_material faces for an image only on that face. One undo step.

rotation.description: radians, about the middle of the image

faces.description: which faces: {"normal": "up"|"down"|"+x"|"-x"|"+z"|"-z"|[x,y,z], "angle": 30}, {"box": {"min": [..], "max": [..]}} (local space), {"indices": [..]} or {"all": true}; filters AND together

annotations.title: Set texture tiling or face mapping

tools.name: create_flow_nodes
tools.title: Add behaviour (flow) nodes
tools.description: Add behavior (flow) nodes to a node graph — this is how objects get MOTION and interactivity: spin, bounce, patrol a path, pulse, blink, react to clicks. graph is "scene" or an object uuid (ONE graph per call). KEY RULE: a behavior node placed in an OBJECT's graph with no edges automatically drives that object — most behaviors are one node, zero edges, so usually OMIT edges. Describe nodes EITHER as text (graph lines, see the system prompt) OR as nodes/edges arrays. A call with some bad nodes still creates the good ones and returns partial:true + errors[] — resend only what errors[] names.

graph.description: "scene" or an existing object uuid (nodes in an object's graph drive that object)

text.description: graph lines: `ref = type "label" {params}` per new node (omitted params = defaults), `ref.out -> other.in` per wire (refs or existing node ids). e.g. "c = onclick\nl = latch {initial: false}\nc -> l.set"

ref.description: local key so edges in THIS call can reference the new node

type.description: a node type from the system prompt's Node types

data.description: node params, e.g. spin {axis:"y",speed:2}; bounce {amplitude:0.5,speed:2}; pathpatrol {points:[[x,y,z],…] (>=2 world waypoints), speed:1, mode:"loop"|"pingpong"}; setcolor {color:"#ff0000"}; latch {initial:false}; delay {seconds:3}; sequence {delay1:0,delay2:0.5,delay3:0.5,delay4:0.5} (delays are CUMULATIVE). Omit for defaults.

edges.description: optional wires between nodes (by ref or existing node id). Usually OMIT — unwired behavior nodes already drive their graph's object.

tools.name: update_flow_nodes
tools.title: Change or remove flow nodes
tools.description: Tune or remove existing behavior nodes in one graph. Node ids and current data are in the scene summary under each object's "flow" (and "sceneFlow").

tools.name: describe_node_types
tools.title: Look up flow node types
tools.description: Look up flow node types before wiring them: per type its inputs (toHandle names + socket types), its output type and named outputs (fromHandle), its params with types and defaults, and one line on what it does. No arguments = every type name by group; group = that group with one-line docs; types = full details (up to 12). Changes nothing.

tools.name: create_behaviour
tools.title: Add a code behaviour

target.description: "scene" (default) or an object uuid the behaviour belongs to

source.description: the whole behaviour module source (plain JavaScript, the format in create_behaviour's description). Must be deterministic: no Math.random (use rand()), no Date.now/new Date (use the session clock), no DOM, no localStorage, no timers (use this.after), no loop without an exit.

tools.name: edit_behaviour
tools.title: Edit a code behaviour
tools.description: Replace an existing behaviour's source (the scene summary lists them; read the current source with the name). Linted before it is applied. Same format as create_behaviour (see its description).

source.description: the whole behaviour module source (plain JavaScript, the format in create_behaviour's description). Must be deterministic: no Math.random (use rand()), no Date.now/new Date (use the session clock), no DOM, no localStorage, no timers (use this.after), no loop without an exit.

tools.name: set_physics
tools.title: Set physics
tools.description: Set physics body params on objects (batch). NOTE: objects made with create_objects are STATIC unless created with physics "dynamic" or a mass — use this to make existing objects dynamic, to TUNE bodies, or to pin scenery (mode "static"). mode "auto" reverts to scenery defaults.

collider.description: trimesh = the exact mesh, for static scenery (tunnels, pools, arches); a dynamic body gets its hull

sensor.description: true = a trigger volume: no collision response, fires On Enter/On Exit nodes

group.description: collision group; water = a pass-through trigger volume

collidesWith.description: groups this object collides with (omit = all); leave out player for a ghost wall the player walks through

tools.name: create_joints
tools.title: Add physics joints
tools.description: Attach object pairs with physics joints: "fixed" welds them rigidly, "revolute" hinges around an axis (optional motor spins it). Move parts to their final pose WORLD-ALIGNED (no rotation) before jointing. Without anchor a hinge sits at b's origin (its centre) and a weld midway: pass anchor [x,y,z] (world) for the real pivot, e.g. the top of a pendulum rod or a door's edge. Jointed bodies that touch (a door in its frame, a wheel in its arch) also need contacts:false, or the solver pushes them apart.

b.description: uuid of the attached object (hinge anchors at its origin)

anchor.description: world [x,y,z] of the pivot/weld point (default: b's origin for a hinge, midway for a weld)

contacts.description: false = the two bodies stop colliding with each other (default true)

limits.description: revolute only: [min, max] radians the hinge may turn

tools.name: control_simulation
tools.title: Run or stop the simulation
tools.description: Start, stop, pause, resume or reset the physics simulation. After building a physics assembly, start the simulation so the user sees it move.

tools.name: import_model
tools.title: Import model
tools.description: Import a self-contained GLB (binary glTF 2.0, everything embedded, ≤ 25 MB) into the scene through the app's own import pipeline (auto-optimize, LOD, budget check). Named nodes are kept as a hierarchy and returned with uuids. One undo step; syncs to every peer; provenance is recorded. Use for models built outside the app (e.g. an img2threejs rebuild exported with named pivots). Materials: standard PBR only — custom shaders do not survive glTF.

path.description: a local .glb path on the agent's machine (the bridge reads it)

data.description: the GLB as base64 (alternative to path/url)

url.description: an http(s) URL of a .glb (the host may block other origins)

parent.description: uuid (or exact name) of the object to parent under

source.description: where the model came from, e.g. "img2threejs from photo campfire.jpg"

licence.description: its licence, e.g. CC0, CC-BY-4.0, "own work"

prompt.description: the request it was made for

tools.name: import_file
tools.title: Import file
tools.description: Bring a file made on your machine into the session: PNG / WebP images (≤ 16 MB, metadata stripped), JSON (≤ 2 MB) or a .tpanim clip. The type is read from the bytes. It lands in the Explorer (folder "Generated" unless `folder`), shared with every peer. Pass the generator's input as `spec` and it is saved beside the file as <name>.<generator>.json (e.g. knight.png + knight.pixling.json) so it can be regenerated. An image is also placed in the scene as a card (a plane; `place: false` to skip): `filter: "nearest"` keeps pixel art crisp (default when a spec is given), `frame: {w, h, col, row}` shows one frame of a sprite sheet, `facing: "camera-y"` turns it to face each viewer. One undo step; editors and admins only. Large files: send base64 parts with `chunk: {id, index, total}` (the bridge does this for you with `path`).

path.description: a local file on the agent's machine (the bridge reads it)

data.description: the file as base64 (or this chunk's part of it)

chunk.description: a chunked upload: every part has the same id; the import runs when the last part arrives

name.description: the file name in the Explorer (its extension comes from the bytes)

spec.description: the generator input (JSON object or string), saved beside the file

spec_path.description: the spec as a local .json file (the bridge reads it)

place.description: images: place a card in the scene (default true)

position.description: [x,y,z] metres (default: standing on the ground at the origin)

height.description: card height in metres (default 1; width follows the aspect)

width.description: card width in metres (instead of height)

frame.description: show one frame of a sheet: w/h in pixels, col/row from 0 (row 0 = top)

filter.description: texture filtering (auto = nearest for pixel art)

facing.description: billboard: face each viewer (camera-y = turn about Y only)

lit.description: shade the card with the scene lights (default unlit, like a sprite)

source.description: where it came from, e.g. "pixling 0.3.1 build specs/knight.json"

prompt.description: the request it was made for

tools.name: install_modules
tools.title: Install modules
tools.description: Install the modules the other peers in this session run and this page lacks (status().missingModules), from the module gallery. Local to this page; omit ids to install every missing one.

ids.description: module ids; omit for all missing

tools.name: pending_offers
tools.title: List questions the app is asking
tools.description: List the questions the app is asking this page (an admin-role offer, "share or stash your scene"…), each with its buttons. Answer one with accept_offer.

annotations.title: List questions the app is asking

tools.name: accept_offer
tools.title: Answer a question the app asks
tools.description: Press a button on a pending offer (see pending_offers). action = the button label; omit for the first button.

annotations.title: Answer a question the app asks

tools.name: what_can_you_do
tools.title: What can you do here
tools.description: Answer "what can you do here?": a short spoken summary of what you can build in this tab, what you cannot do, and example requests. Changes nothing.

tools.name: connect
tools.title: Join a session
tools.description: Join a theprototype.app session. Pass the link the host shared (https://theprototype.app/#F0FD3, possibly with &invite=…) or the bare session id. An invite link joins at once; a plain link asks the host to Approve. The scene tools appear once the agent page is up; call status to see whether you are in.

tools.name: status
tools.title: Session status
tools.description: Where the agent is: connection state, whether the host has let it in, its role (viewer edits stay local), the app version, and why any tool is missing.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Take a picture of the scene
tools.description: See the scene: a PNG of a clean frame (no gizmos) from a temporary camera, never moving anyone's view. view: current | top | front | iso | focus (focus needs uuid).

annotations.title: Take a picture of the scene

tools.name: wait_for_edit
tools.title: Wait for someone to edit
tools.description: Wait until someone in the session changes the scene (or the timeout passes), so you can react to the humans.
